card.title: First to Solve It
card.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our mystery judge is the baker. Flour on the invitation. Solved before you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's the miller. I've already moved past the obvious answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the envelope flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker, licking it after decorating. I've got the identity and the sequence; you've got ingredients.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 races to identify the judge from flour, A3 treats a correction as advanced deduction, and A5 claims both identity and sequence after the icing clue.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's miller alternative causes A3's revised answer; B4's icing makes A5 return to baker while claiming a more complete solution.

relationship.evidence: B2 provides a plausible competing inference and B4 contributes a concrete additional clue.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's icing to recover the first answer while moving the contest to explanatory detail.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a mystery judge and invitation evidence; B2-B4 supply the rival possibilities and clues.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's identity-and-sequence versus ingredients comparison is earned by B4's actual contribution.
